major.title: requireText is not silent in production browser bundles (React, Vue, vanilla)
major.evidence: development() returns `typeof process === 'undefined' || process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'`. A bundler replaces only process.env.NODE_ENV; in a browser `process` does not exist, so the first operand is true. The repository's own production builds contain `try{return typeof process>`u`||!1}` (examples/react/dist/assets/index-*.js, examples/vue/dist/assets/index-*.js, apps/playground/dist/assets/index-*.js). Chromium, esbuild bundle with process.env.NODE_ENV="production" (browser/results.json, scenario missing-production): react 17 "Hawiyah:" warnings, vue 13, vanilla 12, angular 0 (Angular is guarded by ngDevMode). packages/core/test/text.test.ts:34-36 covers only Node with a stubbed NODE_ENV, where process exists. CONTRACT.md:84-86, CHANGELOG.md:43-44 ("production builds stay silent") and packages/core/API.md:346-348 state the opposite.
major.suggestedFix: Drop the typeof guard and rely on the existing try/catch: `try { return process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'; } catch { return true; }` (a bundler folds it to false; without a bundler the ReferenceError means development; __HAWIYAH_DEV__ still overrides). Add a test that evaluates the built core module with NODE_ENV replaced and no `process` global, and keep check:packages tree-shaking budgets.

major.title: Vanilla SearchField discards authored clear-button text and leaves the button unnamed (open point b)
major.evidence: Line 31 reads only options.clearLabel, the button's aria-label and data-hw-clear-label; line 34 replaces the button children with an icon. Chromium (browser/results.json, vanillaPrecedence.s1): `` becomes ``, aria-label null, text "", one warning "SearchField requires \"clearLabel\"". Rule 7(1) of m2-spec.json and packages/vanilla/README.md:44-45 say the text or aria-label already on the element is used as written. Before the milestone the control always had a name (built-in default). tests/search-field-parity.test.ts:85 and tests/search-suggestions-vanilla.test.ts mount exactly this markup and do not assert a name.
major.suggestedFix: Before replacing the children, take the name from the authored text when there is no aria-label: clearLabel = options.clearLabel ?? aria-label ?? trimmed textContent ?? data-hw-clear-label (the order used by PasswordField in controls.ts:16), write it as aria-label, and restore the text on destroy (already done). Add an assertion to the two tests.

minor.title: Open point (a): CONTRACT.md states the vanilla precedence in the wrong order; the code is right
minor.evidence: m2-spec.json rule 7: "(3) the controller option of the same name, which wins over the attribute"; packages/vanilla/README.md:51 and CHANGELOG.md:35-38 say the same; dom.ts:49 is `value ?? root.getAttribute(dataName(name))`. Chromium (results.json vanillaPrecedence): option + data-hw-label -> aria-label "OPTION" and page button "OPTION 1"; authored aria-label + attribute + option -> "MARKUP". Only CONTRACT.md lists "authored markup, data-hw-<name>, then the controller option" as one order, which reads as attribute before option. Secondary: an explicit option overrides authored markup in SearchField (search-field.ts:31, measured "OPTION" over aria-label="MARKUP"), PasswordField (controls.ts:16) and PortalHeader brandLabel (portal.ts:28), while root names (dom.ts nameRoot) and PortalHeader menu/navigation (portal.ts:22-23) keep the markup.
minor.suggestedFix: Change the contract, not the code: "Vanilla uses authored markup as written; otherwise the controller option of the same name; otherwise data-hw-<name> on the controller root." State in the same sentence whether an explicit option may replace an authored name, and make the three controllers above follow it.

minor.title: Open point (c): Angular warnings name the selector; documented for Angular only

The parity test accepts both with /(FileDropzone|hw-file-dropzone)/.
minor.suggestedFix: Keep the selector (it is the name an Angular developer writes; the class is HwFileDropzoneComponent, not FileDropzone) and record it: one sentence in CONTRACT.md ("the component is named as the adapter exposes it: the selector in Angular"), a note in m2-reconcile.json, and an exact per-adapter expectation in the parity test.

minor.title: Open point (d): Angular SearchField shows the search button by default, so searchLabel is needed by default there

Documented in packages/angular/README.md:287 and docs/nic-search.md:40-41, absent from m2-reconcile.json parityGaps.

Record it as a parity gap now; in milestone 3 change the Angular default to false (breaking, CHANGELOG entry) so that the same markup behaves the same in three adapters. If the default must stay, make searchLabel @Input({required: true}) in Angular so the type reports it.

minor.title: Angular field templates render an empty <label> and placeholder="" when the optional text is absent
minor.evidence: fieldLabel is `<label class="hw-label" [for]="controlId">{{ label }}…</label>` without a condition, used by nine templates; only hw-file-dropzone (advanced-controls.ts:361) and hw-date-picker (:287) were guarded. Chromium, hw-search-field without label: empty label.hw-label and placeholder="" on the input (results.json angular.missing emptyNamed, badAttr). Rule 12: a missing text renders nothing and the attribute is omitted.
minor.suggestedFix: Wrap fieldLabel in @if (label) and bind [attr.placeholder]="placeholder || null" in the three templates, as forms.ts:58 already does.
